title: Push step-count axis further (TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2^18->2^17)
description: Halved TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE from 2^18 to 2^17 and DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE from 128 to 64 (grad_accum_steps=1), doubling optimizer steps again within the fixed 5-min budget on top of the current baseline (ASPECT_RATIO=96, WEIGHT_DECAY=0.1, DEPTH=8).
reflection: This is the experiment proposed twice before (round 3 by a0 and a4) but abandoned both times in favor of other axes -- pivoted away from my own crowded WARMDOWN_RATIO=0.7 proposal (duplicated by a5) to run this instead since only a2 proposed it this round. Result: val_bpb 0.978041 vs baseline 0.982306, a genuine ~0.43% win, clearly outside the ~0.02-0.03% noise band this cell has repeatedly shown. The step-count axis had more room after all -- going from 2^19->2^18->2^17 has now given three consecutive real wins (1.001->0.999 alone, 0.9986->0.9826 stacked with width, and now 0.9823->0.9780), suggesting this fixed 5-min-budget regime strongly favors more, smaller, noisier optimizer steps. Worth testing whether it extends further to 2^16 in a future round, and whether the WEIGHT_DECAY=0.15 bracket (proposed 3x this round) should now be re-run on top of this new baseline rather than the old one.
